Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for adult female reporting 7 days of fever with alternating chills/hot sweats, myalgias, nausea, reduced oral intake, and fatigue after recent travel to rural and urban areas in Vietnam; plan for urgent in-person evaluation and blood tests including malaria thick/thin films.

History:
- Presenting complaint: 7 days of fever with sweating (including night sweats), intermittent chills, generalized myalgias, nausea, reduced appetite, low fluid intake, and fatigue.
- Timeline: Onset ~7 days prior; persistent symptoms with only slight temporary relief from OTC antipyretics.
- Modifying factors: OTC ibuprofen and paracetamol (acetaminophen) provide slight symptomatic relief.
- Associated symptoms: Night sweats; feels alternately hot and cold; fatigue.
- Pertinent negatives: No cough, cold symptoms, or sore throat; no ear pain; no diarrhea; no neck stiffness; no new/worsening headaches beyond baseline; no rash; no swollen/tender joints (chronic back pain noted); no dysuria; no increased urinary frequency.
- Travel history: Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago; visited multiple regions including countryside and cities; trekking and cycling with rural/farmland exposure; took malaria prophylaxis (daily regimen and an additional tablet; specific names not recalled).
- Occupational impact: Difficulty working due to fatigue.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic back pain: Attributed to prolonged sitting/poor posture; under active physiotherapy; exercises focused on posture and back strengthening.
- Headaches/migraines: Patient states chronic screen- or weather-related headaches; initially denied migraines, later reported sometimes struggling with migraines (conflict noted).
- No other major illnesses reported.

Medications:
- Seroxat (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Ibuprofen OTC (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Paracetamol/acetaminophen OTC (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Malaria prophylaxis during Vietnam travel (specific agents, dose/route/frequency not documented).

Allergies:
- Pollen (hay fever). Denies medication allergies.

Social History:
- Occupation: Nurse; reports being up to date on vaccinations including Hepatitis B.
- Tobacco: Non-smoker.
- Alcohol: Moderate intake.
- Exercise: Moderate exercise a few times per week.
- Travel: Vietnam, returned 4 weeks ago; rural/farmland exposure; trekking and cycling.

Family History:
- Father: Myocardial infarction at age ~68 (deceased).

Physical Examination:
- 

Investigations:
- None completed at time of consult.
- Planned: Thick and thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; additional blood tests to be determined after in-person examination.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Febrile illness of unclear origin in a recent traveler (Vietnam) with night sweats, myalgias, nausea, and rural exposure; malaria and other travel-related infections need exclusion.
  - Plan:
    - Urgent in-person clinical examination at central London clinic (preferred by patient) to determine urgency of investigations.
    - Blood tests including thick and thin blood films for malaria and inflammatory markers; further tests as guided by examination findings.
    - If unable to attend central London, patient may attend local A&E; clinician’s note to be shown at reception outlining requested tests.
    - Work exclusion: Do not attend work until evaluation completed and cause clarified.
    - Administrative: Clinician to message admin to book appointment; patient to call provided number to confirm same-day slot.
- Issue 2: Chronic back pain related to posture; under physiotherapy.
  - Plan:
    - Ongoing management with physiotherapy; no changes discussed during this consult.

- General plan items:
  - No new prescriptions issued.
  - Safety/urgency of testing to be determined after in-person exam.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs; physical examination; medication doses/routes/frequencies; detailed malaria prophylaxis names/regimens; pregnancy status; comprehensive sexual history; full review of systems; baseline medical history beyond items listed.
- Internal conflicts: Headache history—patient initially denied migraines but later stated she sometimes struggles with migraines (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor pauses/false starts but clinically adequate.
